action:
# Select all text in the document to prepare for font change
pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'a')

# Click the empty font-name field in the formatting toolbar to activate it
pyautogui.click(x=300, y=100, duration=0.5)

# Click the "Close Preview" red X button in the print-preview toolbar to return to normal edit mode
pyautogui.click(x=520, y=103, duration=0.5)

# Click the red “Close Preview” (X) button on the Print Preview toolbar to return to editable mode
pyautogui.click(x=516, y=104, duration=0.3)

# Exit Print Preview mode using the toggle shortcut (Ctrl+Shift+O)
pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'shift', 'o')

# Select all text in the document so the upcoming font change applies globally
pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'a')

# Click the blank font-name input box in the formatting toolbar to focus it for typing the new font
pyautogui.click(x=286, y=104, duration=0.5)

# Click the red “Close Preview” (X) button on the Print Preview toolbar to return to edit mode
pyautogui.click(x=507, y=104, duration=0.3)

# Exit Print Preview mode so the standard formatting toolbar (including font box) is available for editing
pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'shift', 'o')

# Select the entire document so the upcoming font change applies globally
pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'a')

# Click the empty font-name field in the formatting toolbar to focus it for typing “Times New Roman”
pyautogui.click(x=286, y=104, duration=0.3)

# Exit Print Preview mode (so formatting toolbar with font field becomes accessible)
pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'shift', 'o')

# Select all document text so the forthcoming font change applies to entire document
pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'a')

# Click the blank font-name field on the second toolbar row (right of the “normal” style dropdown) to focus it for typing Times New Roman
pyautogui.click(x=270, y=129, duration=0.3)

# Type “Times New Roman” into the focused font-name box and press Enter to apply it
pyautogui.typewrite('Times New Roman\n', interval=0.05)

# Undo the accidental insertion to restore original document content
pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'z')

# Undo again to restore the full document content before the unintended replacement
pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'z')

# Undo once more to continue restoring the full original document content
pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'z')

# Undo again to keep restoring the full original document content
pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'z')

# Undo again to further restore the document content toward its original state
pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'z')

# Continue undoing changes to recover full original document content
pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'z')

# Continue undo sequence to restore the original multi-page document content
pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'z')

# Click the blank font-name box in the formatting toolbar (right of “normal” style) to focus it for entering "Times New Roman"
pyautogui.click(x=280, y=104, duration=0.3)

# Click the red “Close Preview” (X) button on the Print Preview toolbar to exit preview mode and return to editable view
pyautogui.click(x=515, y=104, duration=0.3)

# Click the red “Close Preview” (X) button in the Print Preview toolbar to return to normal editing mode
pyautogui.click(x=505, y=104, duration=0.3)
pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'shift', 'o')

# Select the entire document content to apply the font change universally
pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'a')

# Click the blank font-name field (to the right of “normal” style dropdown) to focus it for entering the new font
pyautogui.click(x=310, y=104, duration=0.3)

# Exit Print Preview mode using the shortcut so formatting toolbar with font box reappears
pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'shift', 'o')

# Select all text in the document so the forthcoming font change applies everywhere
pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'a')

# Click the empty font-name input box (to the right of the “normal” style dropdown) to focus it for typing the new font
pyautogui.click(x=290, y=104, duration=0.3)

# Exit Print Preview mode so the normal formatting toolbar (with font box) reappears
pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'shift', 'o')

# Select the entire document content so the forthcoming font change can be applied to everything
pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'a')

# Click the font-name input box (to the right of the “normal” style dropdown) to focus it for typing the new font
pyautogui.click(x=230, y=104, duration=0.3)

# Click the “Cancel” button at the top-left of the Save dialog to close it and return to Writer
pyautogui.click(x=303, y=73, duration=0.3)

# Click the “Cancel” button in the top-left corner of the Save dialog (to close the dialog and return to Writer)
pyautogui.click(x=265, y=73, duration=0.3)

# Click the "Cancel" button at the top-left of the Save dialog to close it and return to the document
pyautogui.click(x=310, y=72, duration=0.3)

# Close the interfering Save dialog by pressing Escape
pyautogui.press('esc')

# Click the blank font-name field (right of “normal” style dropdown) in the formatting toolbar row to focus it for typing the new font
pyautogui.click(x=310, y=129, duration=0.3)

# Click the empty font-name field (immediately right of the “normal” style dropdown) to focus it for entering “Times New Roman”
pyautogui.click(x=250, y=104, duration=0.3)

# Click the grey “Cancel” button in the Print dialog to close it and return to the document
pyautogui.click(x=915, y=585, duration=0.3)

# Dismiss the modal Print dialog to return to editing mode
pyautogui.press('esc')

# Click the blank font-name box on the Formatting toolbar to focus it for typing the new font
pyautogui.click(x=280, y=130, duration=0.3)

# Type “Times New Roman” into the focused font-name box and press Enter to apply it to the selected text
pyautogui.typewrite('Times New Roman\n', interval=0.05)

# Undo the accidental overwrite to begin restoring original document content
pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'z')

# Continue undoing to restore the original full document content before attempting font change
pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'z')

# Undo again to continue restoring the original multi-page document content
pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'z')

# Continue undoing to restore the full original document content before applying the font change
pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'z')

# Undo again to further restore the original multi-page document content
pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'z')

# Continue undoing to retrieve the original multi-page document content
pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'z')
